newsitem.title: USA: Ethics panel expands investigation of Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Ethics panel expands investigation of Gingrich.

text.p: The House ethics committee said Thursday it had expanded the scope of a long-running investigation of charges against House Speaker Newt Gingrich.
It said it had uncovered "certain facts" that merited further inquiry, including whether Gingrich had provided "reliable, accurate and complete information" about a course that he taught.
The development came as House Democrats kept up a drumbeat of demands that the ethics committee release a report it received on the Gingrich investigation last month.

Special counsel James Cole has been investigating whether the financing by tax-deductible contributions of college courses Gingrich taught in Georgia violated federal laws barring tax-exempt charities from furthering partisan politics.
In a statement the committee said the investigation had been expanded to cover four areas.
These were:
- Whether Gingrich "provided accurate, reliable and complete information," either directly or through counsel, related to his course "Renewing American Civilisation."
- Whether his relationship with the Progress and Freedom Foundation violated the foundation's Internal Revenue Code status.
- Whether Gingrich's use of the personnel and facilities of the Progress and Freedom Foundation constituted a use of unofficial resources for official purposes under House rules.
- Whether his activities on behalf of the Abraham Lincoln Opportunity Foundation violated its IRS status and whether the foundation violated its status with Gingrich's approval and knowledge.

In a three-page interim report, the committee said its action in expanding the inquiry did not mean that the investigating subcommittee had found any reason to believe Gingrich had committed any violation.
It said the panel would try to finish its work as expeditiously as possible and expected to complete the process by the end of the present Congress - in early January.

"Newt Gingrich's speakership is beginning to unreval," Gingrich's chief Democratic critic, Representative David Bonior, of Michigan, said. "Today, Newt's worst nightmare came true. The ethics committee that has protected him for two years has decided that they can't protect him any longer."
Bonior said the vote of the ethics committee Thursday to issue its interim report confirmed that charges against him were the "tip of the iceberg."

In a statement on behalf of Gingrich, the speaker's press secretary Tony Blankley said the committee's action refuted claims by its top Democrat, Jim McDermott of Washington, that the ethics process had broken down.
At a news conference last week McDermott suggested that the investigation was being deliberately delayed.

Noting the committee had emphasised there had been no finding of any violation, Blankley said: "I am confident the committee will conclude this matter to be groudless, as it has hundreds of other Democrat charges against the speaker."

In a letter to committee chairman Nancy Johnson, R-Connecticut Thursday, Gingrich called for release of the interim report and said he had submitted 46,000 pages of documents and spent 11 hours in interviews with Cole and would continue to cooperate.
Bonior and other Democrats have been demanding the release of Cole's report, charging that a coverup was under way.
But Johnson said last week it would be made public in accordance with the rules when the subcommittee had completed its work and sent its report to the full committee.
She asked for an end to "political interference."
